clue.text: Explorer appreciated source of medicine in medical facility

parts.note: TA is informal British for thanks, said when something is appreciated

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece is placed within another
a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: An explorer grateful to find a supply of medicine at a remote clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appreciated' looks like a verb about the explorer, but it is British slang for thanks. A sanatorium is often shortened in crosswords, and the medicine's initial sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel Tasman was the Dutch navigator who charted Tasmania and New Zealand, so he is an example of a famous explorer.

clue.text: Belief almost widely prevalent in holiday destination

indicators.note: almost all of the word, so it loses its last letter

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief

explanation.surface: A faith that has spread almost everywhere in a popular resort.
explanation.walkthrough: TENET 'almost' drops its final T. Tenerife is the largest of Spain's Canary Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenerife, in the Canary Islands, is a favourite sunshine spot for European tourists.

clue.text: Team supported by country lacking a finesse with the ball?

indicators.note: in a down entry, being supported means sitting on top, so the first piece comes above the second
lacking means going without, so a letter is removed from the word

explanation.surface: A team backed by a nation that can't play the ball with any skill.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAIN without its A becomes SPIN, placed below SIDE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidespin is the sideways rotation a skilled player puts on a ball to make it swerve, an example of deft ball control, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A place selling cheese in turn got in a bad way

indicators.note: to turn round is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a delicatessen sells cheese among other foods

explanation.surface: A cheese shop that has gradually gone downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: A stays put; DELI is written backwards after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to be sick or troubled, so having ailed is to have fallen into poor health.

clue.text: Prominently publish odds on disgraced Swiss official losing face

indicators.note: on puts the odds before the official's name

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds at the off

indicators.note: the face of a word is its first letter, which is lost

parts.note: Sepp Blatter, the Swiss FIFA president who left in disgrace

explanation.surface: Newspapers splash the betting on a scandal-hit football boss's fall.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is the bookmakers' starting price. Sepp Blatter ran FIFA, world football's governing body, until a corruption scandal; 'losing face' drops his B.
explanation.definitionFit: To splatter a story is to splash it across a page, giving it prominent coverage.

clue.text: Play opens dourly in a laboured style

indicators.note: to play with something is to toy with it, so the letters get moved around

explanation.surface: A stage drama that begins in a gloomy, heavy-going manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like the theatre noun, but it is an instruction to rearrange the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ponderous writing or speech is dull and heavy, so doing something this way means with plodding, effortful slowness.

clue.text: A mixture of peas and tripe for an early dish?

indicators.note: a mixture combines ingredients jumbled together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, without the 'and'

explanation.surface: A recipe combining peas with offal, served at the start of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' simply joins the two words of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter served before the main course comes first in the meal, hence an early dish.

clue.text: Money required around a hotel on island for Middle East dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means following after, so the next piece is added at the end
to go around something is to surround it, so letters sit inside another word

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Cash needed for a hotel stay on an island, to buy a Levantine meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money' as tin is old British slang; 'hotel' comes from the NATO phonetic alphabet. The island letter is tacked on last.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahini is a sesame-seed paste eaten across the Levant, an example of a food from that region.

clue.text: Restrict the supply of liquid in rota

indicators.note: something liquid flows and has no fixed shape, so the letters can be poured into a new order

explanation.surface: Limiting drinking water by putting people on a schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' reads as part of the definition, but it is the anagram signal; the definition stops at 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ration is to limit how much of something each person may have, a direct synonym for restricting its supply.

clue.text: Treatment for one largely dull, small swelling

indicators.note: the letters get treatment, worked over into a new order
largely means most of the word, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A remedy for someone mostly feeling flat with a little lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' trims DULL to DUL; with ONE, 'Treatment for' rearranges the six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nodule is a small rounded lump or growth, as on a plant root or in body tissue.

clue.text: Instant record of events showing offhand heavy drinker grabbing husband

parts.note: a snap judgement is made quickly without thought

indicators.note: to grab is to clutch something inside one's grip, so one piece holds another

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A casual drunkard caught holding onto a husband, shown in a quick record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offhand' here means hasty or unconsidered, as in a snap decision, rather than rude.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quickly taken photograph, and figuratively a brief picture of a situation at one moment.

clue.text: With no end of hoo-ha, suspect decrease in digs, say

indicators.note: suspect letters are dodgy, not to be trusted in their order
with no means the named letter is absent from the shuffled letters
the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the word whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A fuss-free note that a dubious fall in value has hit lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of hoo-ha' is A; 'With no' takes it out of DECREASE IN, and 'suspect' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is British slang for lodgings, an example of a residence or place to live.

clue.text: Some not present presumably? That's somewhat stupid

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal: if some are absent, the whole group has not turned up
second meaning: an idiom for being a bit dim or mentally lacking

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally, as a roll call with absentees; the second takes the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone slightly simple or not fully sharp, as if part of their mind were missing.

clue.text: Time taken by a number to comprehend good Latin American dance

indicators.note: to comprehend is literally to take in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
NO is the abbreviation for number
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A time spent by one routine trying to grasp a fine dance from Latin America.
explanation.walkthrough: NO holds G to give N(G)O, after T and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance that originated in Buenos Aires and Montevideo, an example of a South American dance.

clue.text: Liar's outfit is shoddy — typical of one making advances?

indicators.note: shoddy means badly made, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A cheat's clothes are cheap, as you'd expect from someone trying to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making advances' looks like progress, but it means romantic overtures.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone flirtatious behaves playfully towards a person they fancy, which is the manner of a would-be suitor making romantic overtures.

clue.text: Fine line shown in proposal for one making late arrival on the square?

definitions.text: one making late arrival on the square?

indicators.note: to be shown in something is to appear inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a tender is a formal offer
A1 means first-rate, written with an I for the 1
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A proposal made in neat writing, for someone who turns up late at the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the square is the central pitch area, and a tail-ender is a weak batsman who comes in near the end of the innings; the town square is the false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail-ender bats at the bottom of the cricket order, so they walk out to the pitch late in the innings.

clue.text: Undergraduates, maybe, of French engaged in antics

indicators.note: to be engaged in something is to be caught up inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: stunts are daring or showy tricks

explanation.surface: University undergraduates, perhaps, getting up to French pranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' flags the definition as an example: undergraduates are one kind of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Undergraduates are one kind of people studying at a university or college, an example signalled by 'maybe'.

clue.text: Brother in France adopting English at home gets total latitude?

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A French monk who takes in an English child and lets them stay, giving full freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latitude' tempts towards geography, but here it means freedom. Being at home is a common crossword way to say in.
explanation.definitionFit: Free rein comes from loosening a horse's reins; latitude here means scope or freedom of action, not the map line.

clue.text: Difficult American turncoat with no independent source of pictures?

indicators.note: with no means without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: ill can mean hard, as in ill to please
US is the abbreviation for American
I is the abbreviation for independent, removed from the turncoat

explanation.surface: A awkward American defector who lacks any independent supply of images.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAITOR loses its I to give TRATOR. 'ill' meaning hard is an old sense, kept in phrases like ill at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: An illustrator draws the images for books and magazines, so is a person who produces them, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Request to enter a filming location in US state

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece goes within another

explanation.surface: Asking permission to get into a film set in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The filming location is Los Angeles, home of Hollywood, split around the request.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the largest of the fifty United States, an example of an American state.

clue.text: Overly formal type for all to see amid trips abroad

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside another
abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all

explanation.surface: A stuffy person who wants everything public during holidays overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips abroad' looks like foreign travel, but 'abroad' tells you to rearrange TRIPS. U is the British film rating for viewers of all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A purist insists rigidly on correct traditional rules, so is a stickler or pedant about proper form.

clue.text: Thing used by jewellers to examine ring, we hear

definitions.text: Thing used by jewellers to examine

indicators.note: what we hear is speech, so the word is judged by its sound not its spelling

parts.note: a loop is a ring shape

explanation.surface: A tool jewellers use to inspect a ring, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like the item being examined, but it is the sound source: a loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A loupe is a small magnifying glass held to the eye, used by jewellers and watchmakers for close inspection.

clue.text: Only depot sadly with nothing for new miniature dog

indicators.note: sadly, as in badly, so the letters are put in a poor order
with introduces the swap that follows
nothing goes in for, replacing, the letter for new

explanation.surface: A tiny dog found alone and miserable at a depot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' nothing 'for' new turns the N of ONLY DEPOT into O, giving OOLYDEPOT, which 'sadly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The toy poodle is the smallest size of poodle, a tiny breed of dog.

clue.text: A group in part of autumn commercial

parts.note: OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October

explanation.surface: A band featured in a seasonal advert.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is vague: the answer is specifically a group of eight, but any group fits the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An octad is a set of eight things, so it is a particular kind of collection or set.

clue.text: One doing twist in flexible roles, nothing less

definitions.note: to do someone is slang for cheating them, so one doing is a cheat

indicators.note: the twisting word goes in among the other letters
flexible letters bend into a different order
less means the zero is taken away

explanation.surface: A performer twisting into adaptable parts with nothing missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One doing' hides the slang sense of doing someone, cheating them. 'flexible' and 'less' make SLER from the roles minus nothing, with the twist put 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler cons people out of money, which in slang is doing them.

clue.text: Position adopted among hardest ancestors

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A position taken by the toughest of our forebears.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two final words.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is an attitude or opinion someone takes on an issue, or a way of standing, both meaning a position taken.

clue.text: Legal authority in New York worked on treaty

indicators.note: something worked has been shaped by labour, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A New York lawyer who has worked on an international agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York' looks like a source of NY, but it marks the definition as American usage: an attorney is the US word for a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Attorney is the American term for a qualified lawyer who acts in court, so it is what a lawyer is called there.

clue.text: Excessive amount found by academic about The Origin of Species? That's probable

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: an origin is where something begins, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A professor writing too much about Darwin's famous book, which seems likely.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic title tempts one to think of Darwin, but only its 'Origin' matters: the first letter of Species. DON goes around that S. A don is a lecturer at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on describes a bet whose chance of winning is better than evens, hence something likely to happen.
